question: A 45-year-old woman presents to the emergency department due to new-onset symptoms of asthma. She reports that the asthmatic attacks started a week ago. The past medical history includes gastroesophageal reflux disease and hepatitis B. On physical examination, the patient has bilateral foot drop as well as numbness and tingling sensation in all extremities. A complete blood count is relevant for eosinophilia of 9.1 × 108/L. Which of the markers below could explain all of the patient’s current symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Eosinophilia" -> "Allergic reaction" -> "Asthma exacerbation" -> "Bilateral foot drop, numbness, tingling sensation" -> "Peripheral neuropathy" -> "Possible vasculitis" -> "p-ANCA positive in vasculitis" -> "p-ANCA could explain all symptoms" -> 80%

enhanced_information: The presence of eosinophilia in the patient with new-onset asthma and peripheral neuropathy suggests a possible vasculitis. The evidence supports the role of p-ANCA in vasculitis, which could explain all of the patient's current symptoms. Therefore, the marker p-ANCA is the most likely explanation for the patient's presentation.
